other_failure_modes.name: Batch-dependent test features
other_failure_modes.description: Computing features on the test set using operations that depend on the entire test set distribution (like quantile ranks). This makes predictions for a single instance dependent on what other instances happen to be in the test batch, breaking the independence of predictions and making the model unusable for single-instance inference.

other_failure_modes.name: Cross-validation data leakage
other_failure_modes.description: Calculating imputation statistics (like median) and group-by feature aggregations on the entire training dataset before splitting it into cross-validation folds. This leaks information from the validation folds into the training folds, leading to overly optimistic out-of-fold scores.

other_failure_modes.name: Target leakage in out-of-fold encoding
other_failure_modes.description: Using the global target mean or standard deviation (computed over the entire training dataset) as a smoothing prior for out-of-fold target encoding. This slightly leaks the validation fold's target values into the training folds.

summary: The agent has built a highly sophisticated pipeline with a 7-model ensemble, out-of-fold target encoding, and SLSQP-optimized blending. However, the solution contains a critical flaw: it computes quantile ranks directly on the test set, making predictions batch-dependent. Additionally, the agent peeks at the test set to decide on creating missing value indicators, and there is minor cross-validation leakage due to computing medians, group-by aggregations, and global target priors on the full training set before K-fold splitting.
